purpose: Deterministic long-newsletter evidence fixture; all teams, competitions, schedules and results are fictional, and the example URLs must never be fetched as live sources.

topics.headline: Harbor League publishes its season schedule
topics.sourceText: Harbor League published a provisional schedule for eight amateur basketball teams, with the opening round set for October 3 at the fictional East Quay Sports Hall. The schedule lists fourteen regular season rounds, with each team meeting every other team once at home and once away before the standings are finalized. League secretary Mara Fen stated that teams must confirm their venue bookings by September 20, and any unconfirmed home dates will remain provisional until that deadline. The eight listed teams are East Quay, Harbor Central, North Dock, West Pier, Canal Park, Lantern Bay, Market Square and South Basin, according to the schedule. Each Saturday round contains four games, with the first two starting at noon and the remaining two starting at four in the afternoon on separate courts. The published format awards two standings points for a win and one for a completed loss, while a forfeiting team receives no points for that fixture. If teams finish level on standings points, their results against each other decide the order, followed by score difference across those same meetings if necessary. The top four teams are scheduled to advance to a semifinal round on January 23, with first place meeting fourth and second place meeting third. A final on January 30 is listed at the same sports hall, but the announcement does not identify a broadcast partner or promise a live video stream. Each club may register twelve players for the season and dress ten for a game, with roster amendments permitted until the end of the third regular round. Match officials must receive the signed game roster thirty minutes before tipoff, and a player omitted from that document cannot be added after the game begins. The league requires both clubs to appoint a scorekeeper for each fixture, while a separately assigned official will operate the shared clock throughout the game. Postponed games must be rearranged within fourteen days unless the league approves an exception after reviewing a written request from both affected clubs and the venue. Spectator entry is listed as free for regular season fixtures, although the announcement says that capacity restrictions may prevent admission once the hall reaches its posted limit. The organizer will publish a revised schedule if venue confirmations change, and clubs have been instructed to use that dated revision instead of circulating earlier screenshots. The document describes planned fixtures and administrative rules only; it reports no completed games, championship prediction, attendance measurement or independently assessed change in player performance.

topics.headline: River Cup announces its tournament format
topics.sourceText: River Cup organizers announced a fictional twelve-team football tournament scheduled for October 10 and October 11 at Meadow Reach Park, subject to the published weather policy. The teams will enter three groups of four, and each group will play a round robin in which every side meets its three group opponents once. Group matches are scheduled for twenty minutes per half, with a five-minute interval and no additional period if the scores are level at the final whistle. Teams receive three points for a win and one point for a draw, with goal difference and then goals scored used to separate equal group totals. The three group winners and the strongest runner-up will advance to the semifinals, with the runner-up ranking calculated using points, goal difference and goals scored in that order. Knockout matches that finish level will proceed directly to a penalty shootout, and the rules do not provide an extra-time period before those kicks are taken. Tournament director Ivo Reed said that the group draw would be published on October 1 after team registration closes, so the announcement contains no confirmed group assignments. Registered squads may contain sixteen players, and substitutions can be made at approved stoppages after the match official has acknowledged the incoming player's number. A medical station is listed beside the central pavilion, while the event notice asks spectators to keep the marked access lane open throughout both competition days. The weather policy allows officials to suspend play when lightning is observed nearby, with a revised timetable required before any suspended match can resume. The park notice prohibits spectator parking on the neighboring grass field and identifies the north entrance as the only gate available for vehicle access during the tournament. Organizers reported plans and rules rather than results, and the notice supplies no ticket-sales figure, team ranking, verified crowd estimate or claim that a particular club is favored.

topics.headline: Forest Run confirms the course and timing rules
topics.sourceText: Forest Run released a fictional event guide for a ten-kilometer road race on October 18, with the start and finish located inside Cedar Commons Park. The route follows a single marked loop through three named road sections before returning through the park's eastern gate, according to the organizer's accompanying course description. Race director Nela Birch said that the published distance is the organizer's measurement, and the guide does not claim independent certification by a national athletics authority. The first starting group is scheduled for eight in the morning, with a second group leaving five minutes later to reduce congestion on the initial park path. Runners must collect a numbered bib before seven thirty, and the registration table will require the booking confirmation and an identity document matching the registered participant. The timing system will record both the scheduled start and each runner's crossing of the start mat, with the latter used for the published personal elapsed time. Overall podium positions will follow the order in which eligible runners reach the finish, while age-category tables will use the personal elapsed times recorded by the system. Water stations are listed near the third and seventh kilometer markers, and volunteers will direct runners to the correct side of the road as they approach each station. The course guide specifies a two-hour completion window, after which remaining participants must follow instructions from marshals as roads are reopened to ordinary traffic. Participants may report a missing timing result through the event desk until noon, and the organizer will label the first online results table provisional while those reports are checked. The notice recommends that spectators use the park's western pedestrian entrance, because the eastern gate remains reserved for runners and official vehicles throughout the finishing period. No race has taken place in this fixture, and the guide offers no winning time, forecast of individual performance, historical record comparison or medically verified benefit from participation.
